title: A map of the night sky

content.text:
When astronomers describe a star as variable, they do not necessarily mean that it is erratic. Many stars brighten and fade according to a regular rhythm, caused by changes in their outer layers or by the orbit of a companion. The apparent instability is therefore often a clue to an underlying order.

This is why variable stars have proved useful as cosmic markers. If researchers can compare a star’s known intrinsic brightness with how bright it appears from Earth, they can estimate its distance. The method is not effortless: dust can obscure light, and different families of variable stars behave differently. Yet the stars offer a rare measurement tool across enormous stretches of space.

The achievement is less dramatic than a new photograph of a distant galaxy, but it is more foundational. A picture can reveal what is there; a reliable distance tells scientists how the parts of the universe relate to one another. In astronomy, location is not background information. It is part of the explanation.

questions.prompt: What misconception about variable stars does the first paragraph address?

options.text: that their brightness cannot be measured
that every change in brightness is unpredictable
that they are all accompanied by planets
that their outer layers never change

questions.explanation: The writer distinguishes regular variation from erratic behaviour.

questions.prompt: Why can variable stars help researchers estimate distance?

options.text: Their companions reveal the direction of Earth.
Their position is fixed relative to nearby galaxies.
Their known brightness can be compared with their apparent brightness.
Their rhythm becomes faster as they move away.

questions.explanation: The second paragraph states that the comparison supplies the distance estimate.

questions.prompt: The phrase ‘The method is not effortless’ introduces

options.text: technical complications that qualify the method’s usefulness
a claim that the method has been abandoned
an example of a star with no measurable rhythm
a contrast between astronomy and photography

questions.explanation: Dust and different star families complicate, but do not invalidate, the method.

questions.prompt: What does the final paragraph imply about astronomical photographs?

options.text: They are usually more accurate than measurements.
They can be visually impressive without answering every question.
They have made distance calculations unnecessary.
They are useful only for public education.

questions.explanation: The paragraph contrasts a revealing picture with the deeper explanatory value of distance.

options.text: serving as a basis for further understanding
being restricted to the oldest stars
requiring a new kind of telescope
being more attractive to observers

questions.explanation: Reliable distances underpin scientists’ understanding of relationships in the universe.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the text?

options.text: Variable stars are mainly valuable because they produce attractive images.
Regular stellar changes can provide difficult but powerful distance evidence.
Astronomers have solved the problem of measuring cosmic distance.
Dust is the principal reason galaxies are difficult to photograph.

questions.explanation: This captures both the regularity of the stars and the qualified usefulness of the method.
